accessibility.blurb: macOS accessibility keys the rice can actually apply. These write to a TCC-protected domain, so they take effect only when the app you run the rebuild from holds Full Disk Access — otherwise the rice warns and moves on.

agents.blurb: Which coding-agent clients this machine installs, and which one the agent keybinding spawns.

animations.blurb: How much motion macOS spends on its own Dock and windows. The one group in this block that ships **on** — `"system"` leaves macOS's own timings alone (but only stops writing; it doesn't restore values a rebuild already replaced). Deliberately not the Accessibility "Reduce motion" switch, which every browser also reads as `prefers-reduced-motion`.

appStore.blurb: Whether a rebuild may install the roster's `appStoreId` entries. Off by default: it reaches the network and acts on your Apple Account, and it can never be complete — `mas` cannot sign in, and cannot buy a paid app.

apps.blurb: The apps the rice picks for you, and the file types they claim — the ones a finished machine has rather than the ones a room needs to work. Each is one switch you can turn off; what it installs is a roster entry like any other, so you can retune or replace it by app id.

collar.blurb: Touch ID for sudo — including inside a terminal multiplexer — and the passwordless-rebuild rule.

developer.blurb: The developer pack: the CLI toolbelt, Git tooling, coding-agent tooling, and language runtimes. Off is a nebelhaus machine for someone who never opens a terminal by choice.

displays.blurb: Per-display overrides, keyed by which screen you mean.

fonts.blurb: The terminal font. The bar keeps its own font at its own tuned sizes.

git.blurb: Your commit identity, plus the GitHub owner this machine's work lives under — set your own. It stays in [your host file](/internals/flakes/#your-config-is-a-thin-consumer).

homebrew.blurb: How rebuilds treat Homebrew packages you did not declare.

hotCorners.blurb: What each corner of the screen does when the pointer reaches it. Every corner is unset by default, so the rice never overwrites one you set yourself.

hush.blurb: One quiet switch: Do Not Disturb, optional Slack status, and your hooks.

keys.blurb: The keys the rice owns — the leader, the palette, the window-chord modifier — and anything extra you hang off the leader.

locale.blurb: Language, region, units and keyboard layouts. What a rice in any language other than English needs — and the one room whose settings reach apps you already have open, because the rice posts the change notification macOS itself posts.

lock.blurb: Whether waking this Mac needs a password, and how long the grace period is. Worth setting on any laptop that leaves the house.

menuBar.blurb: The stock menu bar: what the clock shows, and which Control Center glyphs sit beside it. (The nebelhaus bar itself is `sill`.)

power.blurb: Sleep timers and Low Power Mode, said separately for battery and charger — which is the whole point, and why this is built on `pmset` rather than on nix-darwin's own power options.

prowl.blurb: Tiling window management and the Caps-Lock leader launcher.

roster.blurb: One list of everything this machine has — apps, fonts, command-line tools. Each entry drives its launcher key, cheatsheet row, and installs it from whichever source it names: a Homebrew cask or formula, a Nixpkgs package, or the Mac App Store.

screenshots.blurb: Where ⇧⌘4 puts its files, in what format, and whether it draws a window shadow or a preview thumbnail. Unset by default, so macOS's own choices stand.

secrets.blurb: Where secret values come from on this machine.

security.blurb: Security posture: the built-in application firewall and how strict it is. Off on a fresh Mac; the setting to turn on for a laptop that joins networks you don't own.

sill.blurb: The menu bar, and which pills it draws.

sound.blurb: Alert volume and sound, interface sound effects, and the boot chime. Volume is 0–100 the way the slider reads it — macOS stores a curve, and the rice does the conversion.

ui.blurb: One number for "make the interface bigger", applied across the rice's own surfaces.

workspaces.blurb: The named AeroSpace workspaces this machine declares, and which roster apps live on each. A workspace, not an app, owns its bar pill and leader throw — so several apps (a whole "comms" role) can share one.
